transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan here from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. Um, I'll kick off — we have Priya, our solutions engineer, on too. How's everyone doing?

[00:12] Marcus (Pegasus): Doing good, thanks. Marcus here — VP Eng at Pegasus Accelerate. We appreciate you carving time.

[00:20] Lina (Pegasus): Hi all, Lina from Cloud Partnerships. Quick intro, we're a cloud-native SaaS that sits on top of spot GPU pools and manage multi-tenant serving.

[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Quick objective for today: orientation + high level compatibility — figure out if there's a fit for a partner integration (onramp, resale, or private deploys). We'll ask about your stack, security needs, pilot timeline, and share how Redwood handles dedicated and private deployments.

[00:47] Marcus: Sounds good. For context — we've been field-testing a managed inference layer and are evaluating two paths: 1) white-label resell of hosted endpoints and 2) deeper on-prem / VPC integration for larger tenants. Security & control are big for us.

[00:58] Jordan: Got it. Could you share a little about typical customers, and expected scale? QPS, model sizes, latency targets?

[01:07] Evan (Pegasus): Yeah, our customers vary. A lot of mid-market SaaS — typical request patterns: 500–2000 qps bursts, tail latency SLO at p95 ~ 200–400 ms for small text gen tasks, but some customers want higher throughput for embeddings and search. We run mixed model zoo — Llama derivatives and a few 70B variants.

[01:28] Priya: Okay that helps. Two quick flags from Redwood side: dedicated capacity maps well to predictable burst windows (reserved GPU pools), while the hosted API is best for lightweight/PLG usage. For your reseller model, the big questions are: how do you want routing & billing to work, and do you need customer isolation via VPC/private control plane?

[01:48] Lina: Isolation for enterprise customers is non-negotiable. We also need audit logs for compliance and a KMS/HSM story for key material.

[01:56] Jordan: Totally. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations; we can surface audit logs and fine-grained RBAC. We'll share the security pack.

[02:04] Marcus: Great. A couple of technical questions up front — how do you handle KV cache persistence when doing private deployments? We want to rehydrate caches across restarts for long-running conversational workloads.

[02:16] Priya: Good question. On Private we provide sticky KV cache persistence options — we can checkpoint to encrypted object storage and rehydrate on node attach. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed) we do in-memory plus optional cache snapshotting into S3-like stores. There are tradeoffs on startup latency; snapshot size matters.

[02:32] Evan: When you say "snapshotting" are those hot-restores or full replays? We've seen issues where rehydration added 300-500ms on cold start.

[02:39] Priya: Usually incremental KV segments to reduce restore time; for large contexts, it's still non-trivial. During pilot we recommend warm pools or pre-warmed nodes for critical tenants.

[02:49] Marcus: Okay. Another angle — quantization. Some of our customers run 8-bit quant models for cost reasons. How does Redwood handle quantized weights and what about perf penalties?

[02:58] Jordan: We support common quant formats and have tuned kernel paths for 8-bit/4-bit variants. Performance depends on hardware and the compilation path; we'll provide model profiles that show throughput/latency tradeoffs. We'll also suggest when to use batching + KV caching to reduce token cost.

[03:15] Lina: Good. From a partnership perspective, Lina here — how would billing work if we're reselling Redwood hosted endpoints? Do you have partner SSO/multi-tenant billing?

[03:24] Jordan: We have reseller models — partner-account mappings and invoice consolidation. For more advanced flows we can do delegated billing via our partner console or via API. We'll get legal to surface a partner annex.

[03:33] Marcus: On network side, we need to know VPC peering and egress patterns. Some customers have strict egress rules and do not allow cross-cloud traffic. Does Redwood support fully air-gapped private deployments?

[03:44] Priya: Yes, for regulated customers we offer an on-prem bundle; it's a heavier lift but supports air-gapped setups. For VPC-based Private, we support VPC/VPN/HSM integrations and you can host the control plane in your environment or a customer-managed account.

[03:58] Evan: Does the on-prem option require specific distro or orchestration? We're mostly Kubernetes-based with a custom scheduler.

[04:05] Priya: We package for k8s (Helm charts + operators) but can adapt to bare metal if needed; some partners run with a lightweight supervisor when k8s is not desired. There can be a small engineering effort for the initial install.

[04:18] Marcus: Thanks. Let's talk about pilot: say we choose a dedicated-reseller path — what is a minimal pilot you recommend?

[04:26] Jordan: Typical pilot: 4–6 weeks. Steps: 1) onboarding + security review, 2) sample workload benchmark (you provide workload), 3) deploy either a dedicated pool or a private instance, 4) validate SLOs and cost per token, 5) sign off and scale. We'll propose a low-cost pilot price on reserved capacity.

[04:45] Priya: Tech-wise during pilot we'll run three benchmarks: latency p50/p95, throughput vs batch size, and cost per 1k tokens for your typical prompts. We'll include quantized model runs if you want.

[04:56] Lina: That sounds reasonable. On the security checklist — SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO (SAML/Okta), and ability to rotate keys via customer KMS. Do you have attestations?

[05:07] Jordan: Yes, we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts; I'll attach them to the follow-up. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC; RBAC and SCIM for user provisioning. KMS rotation can be integrated via API.

[05:20] Evan: Two nitty-gritty items — GPU variants and driver support. We run a mixture of A100 and upcoming H200 instances on partner infra. Any constraints on model compilation/runtime for H200?

[05:32] Priya: We're testing on H200 and have some kernel optimizations, but not all models are equal — we'll provide compatibility notes. For pilot we'll match the hardware you're planning to ship on.

[05:42] Marcus: Pricing — if we resell hosted endpoints, what margin / rev share model do you offer?

[05:48] Jordan: We have tiered partner margin models depending on volume commitments. For Dedicated/resale we provide partner discounts and flexibility. Exact numbers are in the partner pricing annex; I'll ask Partnerships to include a sample.

[05:59] Lina: Would love to see a worked example: 100k tokens/day at p95 300ms using a 13B quant model on A100 — what's the cost delta between hosted vs dedicated?

[06:12] Priya: We'll run that example in the benchmark sheet — we have templated calculators. We'll include both with and without persistent KV cache, since cache can change token counts significantly.

[06:22] Marcus: Great. Any regulatory red flags we should know about for EU customers? Data residency? Logging?

[06:29] Jordan: We can pin deployments to EU regions and provide logs with retention controls. For private deployments, data never leaves the customer's VPC. We'll document data flows for legal and privacy teams.

[06:38] Evan: Quick question re: SDKs & integration cadence — we prefer a server-side SDK in Python + Go. Do you have clients and is the API stable?

[06:46] Priya: Yes we provide SDKs (Python, Go, Node) and a stable REST interface. We publish changelogs and versioned API. For partners we can provide early-access branches.

[06:57] Marcus: If we move forward, what does a typical timeline look like from LOI to GA?

[07:03] Jordan: For a reseller pilot, LOI to pilot in 4–6 weeks; pilot to GA depends on outcomes but often 2–3 months. For private/on-prem there is more lead time — 6–12 weeks for integrations and security approvals.

[07:12] Lina: Alright. Would love to schedule the technical deep dive — specifically VPC peering, KMS flow, and Helm install requirements. Priya, you can lead?

[07:20] Priya: Yup happy to. I'll send 2x 60-minute slots next week.

[07:25] Marcus: One more: when you talk about automatic fallback you mentioned routing between model variants — can you clarify?

[07:31] Priya: Sure. Redwood supports smart routing policies — if a primary model or region is saturated we'll route to a compatible model variant or alternate region automatically based on latency/cost policy. It's controllable per-customer.

[07:42] Evan: That could be useful for burst protection. How do you ensure semantic parity across variants? Some of our clients are picky about output differences.

[07:50] Priya: We provide quality monitoring and eval hooks; during pilot we'll set up regression tests on a prompt set to ensure fallbacks meet quality thresholds.

[07:59] Jordan: Ok I can summarize next steps. First, I'll email the partner deck + SOC2 & ISO artifacts + a short partner annex draft. Priya will propose times for a technical deep dive and prepare a dedicated capacity cost sheet. Evan will provide your perf traces and sample prompts.

[08:17] Marcus: Sounds good. Any other questions from the team?

[08:22] Lina: None from me. Excited to look at the pilot numbers.

[08:26] Evan: All good. Quick note — I'll try to anonymize the traces before sending.

[08:30] Jordan: Perfect. We'll also share a benchmark spreadsheet link (note: internal URL) and a short checklist for VPC onboarding.

[08:38] Priya: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the calendar invites and materials.

[08:43] Marcus: Thanks — talk soon.

[08:45] Jordan: Thanks, bye.

[08:47] End of recording.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (names/acronyms). Shared artifacts referenced: Partner deck (link: https://redwood.example/partners/pegasus-deck), Security pack (link: https://redwood.example/security/soc2.zip), Benchmark template (link: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/template.xlsx).
